newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil's Aasgard oil development running to plan.
newsitem.headline: Statoil's Aasgard oil development running to plan.

text.p: Development of the Aasgard oilfield off mid-Norway is running to schedule but the first seven to eight months of 1997 will be crucial for the project's chances of starting production on time, operator Den norske stats oljeselskap AS said on Thursday.
Construction of the Aasgard A production ship, the world's largest production vessel, was well underway at fabrication yards around the world, Statoil said.
The vessel will have a storage capacity for more than 900,000 barrels and the capacity to process 220,000 barrels per day of oil and 24 million cubic metres per day of gas.
The ship's hull is being built by Hitachi in Japan, the separation modules by Kvaerner's Rosenberg yard in Norway and the gas processing and compression modules by Italy's Belleli.
The development plans require the topside modules and hull to be completed by November 1, when hook-up and commissioning are due to begin at Aker Stord.
Design of the topsides was 60 percent complete, Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.
"Everything remains on schedule so far," it said.
First oil in the systems is targeted for August 7, 1998, with full production beginning on October 1.
